Use Tier 2: modify model_design by adding a jointly trained history-interest pooling module to the existing SASRec network. The latest trial reached macro HR@10=0.4975, below the baseline’s 0.505; Electronics and Industrial_and_Scientific declined while CDs_and_Vinyl improved. This suggests testing whether a broader history representation can complement the current sequential features, although the metrics alone do not establish the cause of the plateau.

For each sequence position, compute attention pooling over the item embeddings in its nonpadding causal prefix, using a learned attention query. Add a learned elementwise gate that blends this pooled representation with the corresponding Transformer feature before the existing final normalization and scoring head. The pooled path provides direct access to recurring interests, while the gate lets the network learn how much sequential context each prediction needs. Both paths share item embeddings and receive gradients from the existing ranking loss, forming one jointly trained network per category.

In training_evaluation, preserve the current sampling, transition weighting, optimizer, hyperparameters, and supplied splits so this experiment isolates the representation change. Mask future positions and padding during pooling, and use exactly the same gated representation in validation and the generated predictor. Train all four categories with seed 42, select one checkpoint per category using fixed validation HR@10, and report their macro average; retain the existing dataset routing and host-managed held-out inference.
